instruction: Replace null ONLY with a tape or laser measurement taken in the flat. Never copy an assumed value into a measured field. Re-run scripts/update-desk-joints.py and scripts/check-clearances.py with Blender afterwards; the architecture in source/flat-v18.blend is checked against these values and must be redrawn if they disagree.
origin: x = 0 at the inside face of the left (kitchen/bed) wall, y = 0 at the room side of the kitchen partition, z = 0 at the finished floor. x grows toward the right (desk/wardrobe) wall, y toward the balcony.

assumed.source: CAD footprint carried since V8; never site-verified

measurement_notes.ceiling_reported: 2,630 mm floor to ceiling for the whole flat, reported by the occupant on 2026-10-23. Location and instrument not recorded; spot readings above the desk and wardrobe top are still worth taking.

what_to_measure.room_width_x_at_*: Left wall to right wall, at the given distance from the kitchen partition, measured at 1 m height above the skirting
what_to_measure.room_length_y_at_*: Kitchen partition to the balcony wall, at the given distance from the left wall
what_to_measure.diagonal_*: Floor-level corner to corner; the two diagonals should agree if the room is rectangular
what_to_measure.ceiling_*: Finished floor to ceiling at that location; the wardrobe-top reading decides whether the top crates fit
what_to_measure.right_wall_plumb_offset_at_2200: Horizontal offset of the right wall at 2,200 mm height relative to its foot (positive = leaning into the room)
what_to_measure.skirting_*: Right-wall skirting board profile; the rear posts and wall flanges sit just above and beside it

services.note: Sockets, switches, radiators, heating pipes, data points and window sills are not yet modelled. Record each with wall, centre position and size before drilling or finalising the desk/wardrobe run.
